 The Hon'Ble Shri Justice Anil Kumar Jukanti
 Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.843 of 2012
Judgment:

entities.text:
M/S. Shriram General Insurance Co. ... vs Smt. K. Pushpa And 4
Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed aggrieved by the order dated 30.04.2012 passed in W.C.No.65 of 2010 on the file of the Commissioner for Workmen's/Employees' Compensation and Assistant Commissioner of Labour-II, Hyderabad (for short 'the Commissioner').
2. Heard Ms. T.Padmaja, learned counsel representing Mr. Harinath Reddy Soma, learned counsel for appellant and None appears for respondents.
3. Matter pertains to year 2012, there is no appearance on behalf of respondents/applicants, this Court is not inclined to adjourn the matter and dispose the matter on merits.
4.
Respondents are legal heirs of the deceased.
The deceased K.Maraiah was a driver of lorry bearing No.AP 30T 5929.
On 13.03.2010, while he was proceeding from Hyderabad to Kothoor, he suffered chest pain, while at the steering wheel, and was shifted to Medicare hospital, he died on 13.03.2010.
Lorry is registered in the name of Ch.Anjaneyulu/Opposite Party No.1 (as in W.C.No.65 of 2010).
Commissioner examined A.W.1 and R.W.1.
Exs.A1 to A7 were marked for applicants.
Ex.B1 is Insurance Policy.

Commissioner, holding that deceased was on duty when the incident happened,
awarded a compensation of Rs.5,28,662/-.
5.

It is submitted by learned counsel for appellant/Opposite Party No.2 (Shriram General Insurance Company Limited) that the death of deceased was natural and the vehicle was not involved in any accident.
That insurance company is not liable to pay any amount.
Learned counsel invited the attention of this Court to the judgments relied upon by their counsel in the Court below (extracted in the order of W.C.No.65 of 2010).
It is further submitted that claimant/respondent was not aged 38 years, that the wages adopted by Commissioner was not correct and the amount of compensation arrived at is on higher side.

It is further submitted that when a person dies other than in an accident,
the Insurance Company cannot be mulcted for payment of compensation.
It is also submitted that it is not forthcoming from the pleadings of the claimants that the deceased was appointed as driver (workmen), that no documents are filed to substantiate the claim.
6. It is submitted that Ex.A3-Post Mortem Report does not reveal the cause of death.
It is further submitted that awarding of interest in favour of the claimants from date of filing of claim petition till the date of award is also improper.
It is pointed out that terms of insurance contract have to be strictly construed and that in the present case, the same have not been construed.
It is lastly urged that the order in W.C.No.65 of 2010 is to be set aside as the order is not based on sound reasoning.

sentences.text: 7. Heard learned counsel appearing on behalf of Insurance Company and perused the record.
8. On 13.03.2010, the deceased was driving the lorry bearing No.AP 30T 5929 and he suffered a chest pain.

It is evident from the order at Paragraph No.14 wherein the Commissioner recorded that Police had clearly observed that deceased was at the steering wheel when he suffered chest pain and died on 13.03.2010.
Ex.A3 is Post Mortem Report of Osmania General Hospital, wherein the cause of death was pending, as report of AP Forensic Science Laboratory was to be received.

The Police records reflect that the deceased was at the steering wheel and he suffered chest pain while driving the lorry from Hyderabad to Kothoor and was shifted to Medicare Hospital for treatment and died.
There can be no dispute with regard to the incident of death happening while the deceased was on the steering wheel (driving).
Nowhere, there is a rebuttal that the deceased was not on the steering wheel except an averment that death of deceased was natural and the vehicle was not involved in any accident.
9. Ex.A4 is a copy of Registration Certificate showing that the lorry is registered in the name of Ch.Anjaneyulu who is Opposite Party No.1 in W.C.No.65 of 2010.
Ex.A6 is a copy of driving license of deceased and is valid up to 17.04.2012.
It is observed from the order that RW1 was examined on behalf of Insurance Company.

10. During cross-examination, he admitted that FIR and Inquest report reflected that the deceased was proceeding as driver from Hyderabad to Kothoor, this admission is substantive enough to bring home the fact that the deceased was at the steering wheel when he suffered chest pain and is during the course of employment as lorry driver.
It is a fact that lorry driver was taken to hospital and died on 13.03.2010.
The Commissioner held that death of deceased was as workman within the meaning of the Act and that the death occurred in the course of employment under Opposite Party No.1.

At Paragraph No.16, the Commissioner held as follows:
"...
With regard to 3rd issue, the applicants claimed that the deceased employee was paid wages @ Rs.4,000/- per month by O.P.1, which was disputed by O.P.2.

As such,
I rely on the Minimum Rates of Wages were fixed by the Government of Andhra Pradesh in employment of Public Motor Transport in G.O.Ms.No.83, L.E.T & F (Lab-II) Department dated 04.12.2006.
As per this G.O., the basic wage for a heavy vehicle driver is Rs.4319/-.
The V.D.A. payable as notified by the Commissioner of Labour, A.P., Hyderabad from time to time was Rs.1002.75 paise per month at the relevant time.

The total wage amounts to Rs.5321.75 paise per month and the same amount is taken as wages for the purpose of calculating the amount of compensation.
ii.
The applicants stated that the deceased employee was 38 years of age at the time of accident, which was disputed by O.P.2.
The applicants relied on Ex.A6, driving license in which his date of birth is recorded as 6.5.1966 and by which date the deceased employee has completed 43 years of age.
In the absence of any contrary evidence, the age of the deceased employee is taken as 43 years for the purpose of computation the amount of compensation."

sentences.text: The contentions raised on behalf of Insurance Company have been answered by the Commissioner by proper reasoning.
The age of employee is also taken as per Ex.A6 which is the driving license and the wages as fixed by the Government are considered.
12. This Court does not find any infirmity in the order of the Commissioner directing to deposit a compensation of Rs.5,28,662/-.
Ex.B1 is Insurance Policy of the lorry, there is no dispute with regard to the insurance coverage of the lorry during the said date.
This Court does not find any illegality or perversity in the order of the Commissioner, no interference is necessitated.

13. It is trite to take note of the Hon'ble Apex Court's judgment dealing with the scheme of the Workmen's Compensation Act in Golla Rajanna and Others v. Divisional Manager and Another 1 ,
wherein the Apex Court held as follows:

entities.text: Golla Rajanna and Others v. Divisional Manager and Another 1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "10. Under the scheme of the Act, the Workmen's Compensation Commissioner is the last authority on facts.
The Parliament has thought it fit to restrict the scope of the appeal only to substantial questions of law, being a welfare legislation.

Unfortunately,
the High Court has missed this crucial question of limited jurisdiction and has ventured to re-appreciate the evidence and recorded its own findings on percentage of disability for which also there is no basis.
The whole exercise made by the High Court is not within the competence of the High Court under Section 30 of the Act."
14. For the reasons aforesaid, Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is devoid of merits, same is liable to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
No order as to costs.
15. The amounts if any to be paid to the deceased family, i.e., respondents/applicants shall be paid as per the order of the Commissioner.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
